reasons: Hypothesis drift: the registered question is whether an options-surface arbitrage violation survives the spread and can be captured. The winning strategy explicitly abandons that question — the docstring states it is 'willing to use a box spread that is merely "least bad" when it is flat' and the `_scan_floor_box` routine accepts boxes down to `floor_min_net = -2.0` index points of net *loss*. Trading a structure you know has negative edge is the opposite of detecting a mispricing; it is a cost-minimisation exercise that has nothing to do with the pre-registered proposition.

The dominant economic activity in the winner is not options arbitrage at all — `_maybe_index_fallback` places directional SPX trades off a bar-bias / daily-bias heuristic (momentum / trend-following on the underlying). That is a separate strategy from the one the hypothesis names, so the reported P&L is not evidence about the hypothesis.

Net P&L is negative (-14.96 index points, ~ -$299) and gross P&L is negative before commissions (-5.56 points). Commission of 9.4 points is larger in absolute value than the gross loss, i.e. costs do not merely decide the outcome — they convert an already-money-losing gross into a bigger net loss. Nothing here is capturing anything after the spread.

On the `spx-options-clean` split the correct answer per the pre-registration is 'report nothing and take nothing'. The strategy instead forces 45 trades across 105 sessions (only 30 with exposure), including negative-edge boxes chosen because they score better than nothing. This is exactly the failure mode the hypothesis warns about: 'a rule that finds an arbitrage on a surface that contains none has found its own spread, and that is the single most likely way to fail here'.

The 'floor' logic optimises `net / horizon` (score) subject to `net >= -2.0`. Maximising a per-session loss-per-session ratio is not a detection rule for anything; it is a search for the smallest way to bleed while satisfying an exposure floor. That is a degenerate optimum relative to the hypothesis being tested.
